+title: 'ACPA-1b: Apply the tools:, disallowedTools: and model of the session agent; endpoint tools stay'
+---
+## What
+Spec: ACPA-1 (TestudoApp/features/packages/foundationmodels-acpagent.md). Decision D90 (c).
+
+After ACPA-1a, the session knows its agent (`AgentDefinition`). This task applies its frontmatter to the root session:
+1. `tools:` and `disallowedTools:` (`AgentDefinition.tools`, `.disallowedTools`, `ToolSpec`): filter the capabilities of the session surface in `Sources/FoundationModelsACPAgent/Tools/ToolCatalog.swift` (`sessionSurface`). Use the same `ToolSpec` match that a sub-agent run uses in FoundationModelsAgents, so a root session and a run read a list the same way.
+2. The endpoint tools cannot be removed (D90 c): `agents`, `skills`, `sessions`, `kanban`, `rules` and `runCode` (which gives `files`). Keep one list of these names in `ToolCatalog.swift`. When an `AGENT.md` names one of them in `disallowedTools:` or leaves it out of `tools:`, the tool stays, and the session logs one warning.
+3. `model:`: the model slot of the agent is the start value of the `model` config option (`ConfigOptions.swift`, `selectableSlots`). An unknown slot logs a warning and uses `defaultSlot`.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] A session agent with `tools: [web]` has `web` and every endpoint tool, and no other capability.
+- [ ] A session agent with `disallowedTools: [agents, shell]` has no `shell`, and still has `agents`, with one warning.
+- [ ] A session agent with `model: flash` starts on the flash slot, and the `model` option shows `flash`.
+- [ ] A session agent with no `tools:` has the full surface, as today.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/SessionAgentToolsTests.swift`: one test for each criterion above.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes with no warnings.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #step1
\ No newline at end of file

+    - `ToolSpec`, `ToolMatch`, `ToolVocabulary`, `ToolSelection`, `ToolListKey` and `ToolResolver` are all internal. No public function of the package applies the match to a list of names. The public surface has only `AgentDefinition.tools: [String]?`, `AgentDefinition.disallowedTools: [String]`, and `ToolCatalog.names` / `register(_:_:)`.
+    - The sibling repository main (79f1428) has the same internal types. A newer pin does not help.
+    - `@testable import` is not a correct path for production code.
+
+    Blocker: the card says to use the same `ToolSpec` match that a sub-agent run uses. The task instruction says: when it is not public, stop. I made no change to the source or to the tests.
+
+    The API that is necessary in FoundationModelsAgents (a public entry over the current `ToolSelection` rules, so the root session and a run read one list the same way):
+
+    ```swift
+    /// The result of the `tools:` and `disallowedTools:` rules of one agent
+    /// over a set of tool names that the host gives.
+    public struct AgentToolSelection: Sendable, Equatable {
+        /// The selected names, in sorted order (`ToolSelection.names`).
+        public let names: [String]
+        /// The grant of the `agents` tool, or `nil` (`ToolSelection.agentsGrant`),
+        /// with `AgentsGrant` made public or given as `[String]?`.
+        public let agentsGrant: AgentsGrant?
+        /// `true` when `disallowedTools` denies the `agents` tool.
+        public let deniesAgents: Bool
+        /// One warning for each entry that matches no name
+        /// (`ToolSelection.findings` as `AgentDiagnostic`).
+        public let diagnostics: [AgentDiagnostic]
+    }
+
+    extension AgentDefinition {
+        /// Applies `tools` and `disallowedTools` with `ToolSpec.parse`,
+        /// `ToolVocabulary(catalogNames:hasAgentsTool:)` and `ToolSelection`.
+        public func toolSelection(
+            over names: [String], hasAgentsTool: Bool
+        ) -> AgentToolSelection
+    }
+    ```
+
+    A second question for the person who adds the API: the root session surface is Multitool capabilities (`runCode` gives `files`, `shell`, `web`, `mcp` and others) plus the standalone `skills` and `agents` tools. The names that the session gives to `toolSelection(over:)` must be the capability names, and MCP patterns (`mcp__srv`, `mcp__*`) then match only when the MCP tools of the surface have `mcp__<server>__<tool>` names. Decide this when the API is added.
+
+    Next: add a card on the FoundationModelsAgents board for this API, change the pin after it lands, then run this card again. I did not edit the sibling repository and did not change a pin, as the task instruction says.
